query: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs phase stability and why, with relevance to retaining desirable combinations of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries of the hypothesis, supporting prior evidence, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys the addition of an optimal Al content increases lattice distortion and modifies the local electron concentration to stabilize a metastable FCC matrix, which under service conditions (high temperature, radiation, and cryogenic loading) either remains intact or undergoes a beneficial transformation (such as limited twinning or minor phase adjustment) that sustains high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: A single-phase FCC Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy with a controlled, near-optimal level of Al.
generation.intervention: Adjust the Al content (e.g., varying around an optimal composition such as Al0.3CoCrFeNi) and apply consistent thermomechanical processing.
generation.conditions: Testing across a range of temperatures (from cryogenic to high temperature) and under controlled irradiation or environmental exposure protocols.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions and chemical short-range ordering induced by Al that modify defect interactions and phase transformation thresholds.
generation.mechanism: Al acts as a chemical and structural lever: it increases lattice distortion and shifts the average valence electron concentration so as to favor a metastable FCC phase that resists deleterious phase transitions at high temperatures (ensuring strength and environmental resistance) while enabling transformation-induced plasticity (e.g., twinning) under cryogenic conditions and providing effective defect sinks under radiation exposure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to a baseline alloy with sub-optimal Al content, the optimal alloy will show a more stable FCC structure with minimal unwanted secondary phases over the entire temperature range, exhibit higher yield strength and ductility retention at both cryogenic and high temperatures, and demonstrate reduced radiation-induced defect accumulation.
generation.baseline: An Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy with either too little or too much Al that fails to maintain a stable FCC phase under extreme conditions, resulting in premature transformation (e.g., to BCC or other intermetallics) and degraded mechanical/environmental performance.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to compositions around a critical Al content (approximately near Al0.3 in mole fraction) and to alloys processed under similar thermomechanical histories where the FCC phase is initially formed; deviations in processing or large composition changes may invoke different stabilization mechanisms.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative thresholds for the optimal aluminum concentration, the degree of lattice distortion required, and the specific microstructural changes under various service conditions need further experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of AlxCoCrFeNi alloys with systematically varied Al content around the predicted optimum. Subject these alloys to controlled thermomechanical treatments followed by exposure to high-temperature, radiation, and cryogenic environments. In situ characterization (using synchrotron XRD and TEM) should be performed to monitor phase stability and transformation behavior.
measurements: Phase composition and structural stability (via XRD/TEM)
Mechanical properties such as yield strength, ductility, and strain hardening over the temperature range
Defect density and radiation-induced microstructural changes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with the predicted optimal Al content does not maintain a stable FCC phase under the tested conditions or shows no improvement in the target mechanical or radiation performance relative to the baseline (or if deleterious transformation occurs), the hypothesis will be falsified.

AlxCoCrFeNi High-Entropy Alloys Enable Simultaneous Electrical and Mechanical Robustness at Thermoelectric Interfaces

Abstract: AbstractThe interface between high-performance thermoelectric materials and electrodes critically governs the conversion efficiency and long-term reliability of thermoelectric generators under high-temperature operation. Here, we propose AlxCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys (HEA) as barrier layers to bond Cu-W electrodes with p-type skutterudite (p-SKD) thermoelectric materials. The HEA/p-SKD interface exhibited excellent chemical bonding with a stable and controllable reaction layer, forming a dense, defect-free (Fe,Ni,Co,Cr)Sb phase (thickness of ~2.5 μm) at the skutterudites side. The interfacial resistivity achieved a low value of 0.26 μΩ·cm2 and remained at 7.15 μΩ·cm2 after aging at 773 K for 16 days. Moreover, the interface demonstrated remarkable mechanical stability, with an initial shear strength of 88 MPa. After long-term aging for 16 days at 773 K, the shear strength retained 74 MPa (only 16% degradation), ranking among the highest reported for thermoelectric materials/metal joints. Phase-transition assisted mechanical behavior of TiZrHfTax high-entropy alloys

Abstract: Recent developments of high-entropy alloys with high strength and high ductility draw attention to the metastability-engineering strategy. Using first-principle theory, here we demonstrate that reducing the Ta level in the refractory TiZrHfTax system destabilizes the body-centered cubic (bcc) phase and leads to the appearance of the hexagonal close-packed (hcp) phase embedded in the bcc matrix. The alloying-induced features of the elastic parameters for the cubic and hexagonal structures are mapped out in details, and strong sensitivity to the crystal lattice and chemistry is revealed. Results show softening of the bcc matrix with decreasing Ta concentration which ensures ductile behavior. However, the elastically nearly isotropic hcp precipitates possess enhanced resistance against shear which promotes strengthening of the TiZrHfTax dual-phase system. The present atomic-level insight provides strong evidence to the experimental observation, and emphasizes the significance of quantum-design for advanced multi-phase high-entropy alloys with excellent strength-ductility combinations.
